coverage.notes: All michigan.gov URLs return 403 to scripted downloads, so both documents were read from Internet Archive copies of the exact michigan.gov files (SEL: snapshot 2022-03-07; Profile: snapshot 2025-06-27). SEL: MDE's 'Early Childhood to Grade 12 SEL Competencies and Indicators' (2017): 5 competencies, 18 indicators (1A-5C), age-band benchmarks. Marked guidance_only because the document presents itself as MDE competencies/indicators (the early-childhood part draws on State Board-approved standards); I found no statement that the State Board adopted the K-12 indicators as standards. Reviewer: upgrade to k12_standards if MDE confirms adoption. POG: MDE publishes a 'Profile of a Graduate' (5 abilities). The PDF is undated, so confirm with MDE it is still current.

frameworks.name: Michigan Early Childhood to Grade 12 Social and Emotional Learning (SEL) Competencies and Indicators
frameworks.notes: Read from the Internet Archive snapshot (2022-03-07) of the michigan.gov PDF above; the live site blocks scripted access, so the reviewer should open the live PDF and confirm the 18 indicator codes/titles match. The document is labelled 2017. Five competencies built on CASEL's 2015 definitions, 3-4 lettered indicators each (1A-1D, 2A-2C, 3A-3D, 4A-4C, 5A-5C), with benchmarks by age band from early childhood to grade 12 and strategies for teachers; items here are the 18 indicators only. Adoption year left blank (publication year only; no adoption statement found). The document says the indicators are emerging, not for identifying disabilities or remediation. Titles and summaries are short paraphrases.

items.title: Awareness of their emotions
items.summary: Recognize and understand one's own emotions.

items.title: Awareness of personal traits, strengths and interests
items.summary: Know one's own traits, strengths and interests.

items.title: Awareness of external supports
items.summary: Know which people and resources outside oneself can help.

items.title: Sense of personal responsibility
items.summary: Take ownership of one's own actions and choices.

items.title: Identify and manage emotions and behavior constructively
items.summary: Name emotions and manage them and one's behavior in helpful ways.

items.title: Demonstrate honesty and integrity
items.summary: Act honestly and consistently with one's values.

items.title: Set, monitor, adapt and evaluate goals
items.summary: Set goals, track progress, adjust and review them to succeed in school and life.

items.title: Awareness of others' emotions and perspectives
items.summary: Notice and understand how other people feel and see things.

items.title: Consideration for others and positive contribution to school and community
items.summary: Show care for others and want to improve school and community.

items.title: Awareness of different cultures and respect for human dignity
items.summary: Be aware of cultural differences and respect every person's dignity.

items.title: Read social cues and respond constructively
items.summary: Pick up on social cues and respond in helpful ways.

items.title: Positive communication and social skills
items.summary: Use positive communication and social skills to interact effectively with others.

items.title: Develop and maintain positive relationships
items.summary: Build and keep positive relationships.

items.title: Prevent, manage and resolve interpersonal conflicts
items.summary: Prevent, manage and resolve conflicts with others in helpful ways.

items.title: Use personal, ethical, safety and cultural factors in decisions
items.summary: Weigh personal, ethical, safety and cultural factors when making choices.

items.title: Effective decision-making for daily academic and social situations
items.summary: Develop, apply and model decision-making skills for everyday school and social situations.

items.title: Role in classroom management and positive school climate
items.summary: Take a developmentally appropriate part in classroom management and a positive school climate.

frameworks.name: Michigan Profile of a Graduate
frameworks.notes: Read from the Internet Archive snapshot (2025-06-27) of the michigan.gov one-page PDF (filed under MDE Academic Standards / Michigan Merit Curriculum). It lists five abilities of a Michigan high school graduate and says the profile's characteristics are evident within all of Michigan's academic standards, including the arts and CTE Career Ready Practices. It is not dated and I did not find a State Board adoption record, so the reviewer should confirm with MDE that this is the current official profile. The names Communicate, Collaborate, Argument & Reason, Technology & Tools and Problem Solve come from the document's own graphic. Michigan Virtual's 2026 articles describe district-level portraits and are not state documents.

items.title: Communicate effectively with varied audiences
items.summary: Communicate clearly and effectively with a variety of audiences.

items.title: Collaborate toward a shared goal
items.summary: Work with others to reach a shared goal.

items.title: Use argument and reason
items.summary: Use argument and reason to research, build arguments and critique others' reasoning.

items.title: Use technology and tools strategically
items.summary: Use technology and tools strategically in learning and communicating.

items.title: Problem solve
items.summary: Problem solve, construct explanations and design creative, innovative solutions.
